test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Aryans lived in the land known as ‘Sapta Sindhu’ (Land of the Seven Rivers). Which of the following was NOT a part of it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shipra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Aryans lived in the region known as 'Sapta Sindhu', which means the Land of the Seven Rivers.
 
• The seven rivers that were part of 'Sapta Sindhu' are the Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej, and Saraswati.
 
• Shipra is not one of these seven rivers and is therefore not part of the 'Sapta Sindhu'.
 
• Shipra is a river in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh and is famous for the city of Ujjain which is one of the locations for the Kumbh Mela.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sapta Sindhu**

 
 
• Sapta Sindhu refers to the region of the seven rivers which were mentioned in ancient Indian texts, especially the Rigveda.
 
• The seven rivers include the Indus (Sindhu), Jhelum (Vitasta), Chenab (Asikni), Ravi (Parushni), Beas (Vipas), Sutlej (Shutudri), and Saraswati (which has now dried up).
 
• This region is considered the cradle of the early Vedic civilization.
 
• The term 'Sapta Sindhu' is often associated with the Punjab region of modern-day India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Indus River**
 
 
• One of the longest rivers in the world, flowing through China (Tibet), India, and Pakistan.
 
• It was the backbone of the Indus Valley Civilization, one of the world's oldest urban cultures.
 
• The river is also known as Sindhu in Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Jhelum River**
 
 
• Originates from the Indian-administered territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• Flows through the Kashmir Valley and Pakistan, eventually joining the Chenab River.
 
• It is also known as Vitasta in ancient texts.
 
 
 
• **Shipra River**
 
 
• Located in the central Indian state of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is famous for the city of Ujjain, which is one of the locations for the Kumbh Mela, a major Hindu pilgrimage.
 
• The Shipra is not part of the 'Sapta Sindhu' and was not associated with the Aryan civilization in the same context.
